title: Multimode oscillation and its route to chaos in transverse-mode-coupled optomechanical resonators
authors: Motoki Asano, Lalit Maharjan, Hiroshi Yamaguchi
abstract: Nonlinear oscillators exhibit rich collective phenomena including synchronization, bifurcation, and chaos. Experimentally accessing multimode nonlinear dynamics, however, remains challenging because low-order internal resonances readily induce mode locking and suppress stable multimode oscillation. Here, we demonstrate a transverse-mode-coupled optomechanical platform that combines engineered collective mechanical modes with optically controllable nonlinear interactions. The engineered transverse mechanical modes enable stable two- and three-mode self-sustained oscillations while suppressing trivial low-order internal resonances. By varying the laser frequency, we observe successive beat-frequency fractionalization (Δf/2 and Δf/3), followed by a broadband state exhibiting enhanced trajectory divergence consistent with deterministic chaos. These results establish transverse-mode-coupled optomechanical resonators as a scalable and tunable platform for exploring high-dimensional nonlinear dynamics in interacting mechanical networks.
summary: The researchers utilized a transverse-mode-coupled optomechanical resonator array to study complex nonlinear dynamics. They successfully achieved stable multi-mode oscillations by engineering the mechanical modes to bypass resonance-induced locking. The system was shown to transition systematically from regular multi-mode states through fractional beat patterns into a chaotic broadband state.
main_problem: The challenge of experimentally accessing and studying stable, high-dimensional multimode nonlinear dynamics in coupled mechanical systems while avoiding mode locking caused by low-order internal resonances.
main_result: The authors demonstrated stable two- and three-mode self-sustained oscillations in a transverse-mode-coupled optomechanical resonator, which subsequently transitioned through fractional beat-frequency states into a broadband regime indicative of deterministic chaos.
method: The study employed an optomechanical resonator array, using laser frequency sweeping and time-series analysis (e.g., Largest Lyapunov Exponent estimation) to characterize the system's nonlinear dynamics.
model_or_system: The platform is an elastically coupled array of microbottle resonators fabricated on a silica fiber, coupled to an optical cavity. This system allows for the engineering of collective mechanical modes and the introduction of optically controllable nonlinear interactions.
key_observables: Mechanical power spectral density, minimum resonance detuning ($\Delta D(f)$), beat frequencies ($\Delta f/2, \Delta f/3$), and the Largest Lyapunov Exponent (LLE).
important_parameters: Laser frequency/wavelength, input optical power, and the degree of coupling between mechanical modes.
main_assumptions: The stability of observed multi-mode states is attributed to the engineered transverse modes, which successfully suppress trivial low-order internal resonances.
figures_summary: Figures show the concept and fabrication of the coupled array, power spectral density confirming multiple collective modes, and plots demonstrating the transition from stable multi-mode oscillation to a broadband state accompanied by increasing LLE.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the platform's ability to support stable multi-mode oscillations by avoiding low-order resonances. It then maps the system's dynamics by observing successive spectral fractionalization ($\Delta f/2, \Delta f/3$) as the driving conditions change, culminating in the evidence of deterministic chaos via the LLE analysis.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, scalable experimental realization of exploring high-dimensional nonlinear dynamics, moving beyond simple two-mode systems and demonstrating a controlled route to chaos in a mechanical network driven by optical coupling.
